transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, what brings me in is just... my head feels really foggy lately. Like, I'm a personal care aide, and I've been making all these little mistakes in my client notes. And I keep forgetting what I was just about to do. Which really isn't like me at all. Actually, the other day I was at Mrs. Higgins' house—she's one of my regulars, sweetest lady, makes this amazing lemon pound cake, though I shouldn't eat it because of my cholesterol, you know? Anyway, she has this old tabby cat that just stares at you while you work. I was trying to write down her blood pressure and the cat was just glaring at me, and I totally blanked on the numbers. I mean, I've been doing this job for years, took some college classes for it and everything, but lately it's just... I don't know, it's like wading through mud up there. Have you ever had a cat? They really do look right through you sometimes.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, yeah, I guess I have. Lately, I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's right there as soon as I open my eyes. Which is usually around 5:30, since I like to have time to make my coffee. I actually just bought one of those French presses because my sister swore it makes it taste so much better, but honestly? It’s just a huge pain to clean. All those little wet grounds get stuck in the metal mesh, and then you're rinsing it down the sink and I always worry about clogging the pipes. My landlord is a real stickler about plumbing bills, he sent out this whole memo last month about what we can and can't put in the garbage disposal. 

But, um, anyway... I can still get through my shift just fine. I talk to my clients and do what I need to do, but inside I’m just sad. Just really flat. Kind of like when somebody leaves a soda out on the counter overnight. Do you drink coffee, Doctor? I feel like you guys must run on it with all the hours you work.
Did you notice the memory and concentration problems starting around the same time as this low, heavy mood, or did the foggy thinking begin first?

Yeah, I'd say they pretty much started at the exact same time. This low, guilty, foggy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now. Just all rolled into one. 

A month ago... yeah, that was right around when they started doing all that road construction on Route 9. Have you been stuck in that traffic yet? It is a total nightmare. They shut down two whole lanes right by the grocery store, and they have those giant orange barrels everywhere. I was just trying to turn into the parking lot to get some of those little mandarin oranges—the ones in the plastic cups, you know, because they last so much longer than fresh fruit, and I hate wasting food. Anyway, this guy in a massive red pickup truck just completely cut me off. Didn't even use his blinker. I mean, what is the point of having turn signals if people just refuse to use them? It drives me absolutely crazy. My dad always used to say that driving is a privilege, not a right, and honestly, some people really need to have their licenses revoked. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the memory stuff. Yeah, about a month.
Have you had any recent illnesses, head injuries, new medications, or changes in alcohol or drug use around the time this fogginess started?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hit my head, and I'm not taking any new pills. I barely even drink, maybe just a beer on a holiday or something. Actually, my buddy Greg brought over this craft IPA last 4th of July, one of those ones with the really colorful, artsy labels? It tasted like pine needles and grapefruit, which I guess is the point, but I just don't get the appeal. Why would you want your drink to taste like a Christmas tree? He was going on and on about the hops and the brewing process, and I just nodded along. He actually brews his own stuff in his garage now. His poor wife complains about the smell all the time. She says it smells like old bread baking in a damp basement. They just redid their basement, actually, put down this really nice laminate flooring that looks exactly like real hardwood. I was thinking about putting something like that in my bathroom, because the linoleum is peeling up in the corner by the tub. It's just a tripping hazard at this point. 

But, uh, no... no new meds, no injuries. Just the foggy feeling.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends and family?

Well, yeah, I guess so. I just don't really feel like doing much of anything lately. Even stuff I usually like. Like, I used to go fishing with my brother every other weekend down at the reservoir. He has this little aluminum boat, nothing fancy, just a little outboard motor on it. But last time we took it out, the motor kept sputtering and dying. We spent half the morning just trying to get the thing started, pulling on that cord until my shoulder ached. He said he was going to take it to this guy he knows who fixes small engines, some guy who works out of a shed behind the old bowling alley. Did you know they closed that bowling alley down? It’s a shame, really. They had the best cheese fries there. Just crinkle-cut fries smothered in that fake, bright yellow cheese, but man, it hit the spot after a few games. Now they’re turning the whole lot into, like, luxury condos or something. Everything is turning into condos these days. Where are normal people supposed to live, you know? 

But, um... yeah. I just haven't been going out with him or doing much. I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you had any thoughts of death or wishing you weren't around, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Well, I... I'm not planning to hurt myself or anything like that. I'm really not. But I guess... I don't know, there have been some mornings lately where I just lay there and think, you know, it wouldn't be the absolute worst thing if I just didn't wake up. And honestly, thinking like that really scares me. 

I usually wake up pretty early, around 5:30, because that's when my neighbor's dog starts barking. He's got this beagle mix, I think, and it just howls at everything. The mailman, a squirrel, the wind blowing... it doesn't matter. He just leaves the poor thing tied up on the porch all morning. I actually tried talking to him about it once, just, you know, being neighborly about it. I brought over some of those zucchini muffins I made—I had a crazy amount of zucchini from my garden last summer. They just took over the whole planter box. I planted them next to the tomatoes, which was a huge mistake, because the vines just strangled the tomato plants. I ended up with maybe three decent tomatoes the whole season. And you can't even buy good tomatoes at the store in the winter, they're always so mealy and pale, like they've never even seen the sun. 

But um... yeah. The thoughts. I don't want to do anything to myself, but just waking up and feeling like I don't want to be here... it's scary.

Would you say these feelings and the fogginess have made it hard for you to keep up with your daily responsibilities, like completing your work shifts or taking care of yourself at home, or have you still been able to manage those pretty much as usual?

Yeah, it’s definitely making things harder. I mean, at work, I’m a personal care aide, so keeping track of the clients' routines is really important. Lately, I've had to ask my coworkers to double-check my documentation because I just keep second-guessing myself. One of my coworkers, Sarah, she's really great about it. She’s been working there for like fifteen years, knows everyone’s quirks. She actually just got back from a cruise to Alaska. She was showing me all these pictures of glaciers and whales on her phone. It looked freezing, honestly. I don't know why you'd go on a vacation to be cold. My wife and I went to Florida a few years ago, down near Sarasota, and the sand there was like powdered sugar. You could walk on it all day and it never got hot. We collected so many shells on that trip, we actually bought one of those big glass jars to put them in, but it’s just been sitting in the closet gathering dust. I keep meaning to put it out on the mantle, but the mantle is already cluttered with all these framed photos that need to be reorganized. 

But anyway, yeah, the fogginess... it’s affecting things at home, too. My wife has had to take over paying some of the bills and handling the scheduling because I’m just not as reliable with the details right now. I just can't seem to keep it all straight in my head.
